header.name: Australia v England
header.description: 3rd T20I (N), England tour of Australia at Brisbane, Nov 27 2026

details.text: taken this time! Clears the front leg, looks to heave this wide of mid-on, miscues from low down on the bat. Overton grabs it low and is confident it's carried. Marsh is walking off. The umpires are checking it. Fingers under the ball confirms the TV umpire
good catch! Round the wicket, short outside leg, Harper pulls and it takes a top edge towards mid-on where Overton backtracks very well, takes it over his shoulder. Harper leaves some out there.

finds long-on! Length ball at the stumps, JFM lofts on the up straight down the ground, perhaps slices across it a touch, doesn't get the distance and it's a simple catch. Another frustrating end for Fraser-McGurk

short again, top edge and taken! Superb bowling from Overton. David went for the pull, can't control it, nicely judged catch. David glances at the pitch as he walks off, but think he's been out-done by Overton

bounced out, Overton does it again! Into the pitch at 139kph/86mph and it gets big on Davies as he attempts to heave leg side. Big top edge, loops tamely towards midwicket where Curran steadies himself for a simple catch inside the ring

Chowders picks out long-on! Career-best figures fo Jamie Overton, who shrugs off the blow to the hand to land another one on Australia. Hard length and Chaudhary tries to flat-bat it down the ground, but can't get either the elevation or power to beat the man back

nicks him off, Overton bags five-for! Full, fast and nibbling across the left-hander, Dwarshuis chases the drive and simply nudges an outside edge into Cox's gloves! Overton celebrates with his arm pointed skyward, like prime Alan Shearer but with much bigger shoulders. Haway the Barnstaple Bomber

floated up, spins and takes the edge! Zampa flails blindly for the final time as the nick netles in Cox's gloves. Up goes Nogajski's finger and Dawson has a third. For the first time tonight, a wicket falls with no Jamie O involvement!

full toss nudged into the leg side... and Owen runs himself out looking for two! So the answer to that question is quickly provided. Salt was racing in from deep midwicket, fired in the throw with Owen on the turn - and even with a full-length dive he can't beat Cox to removing the bails

sliced and diced, the bails go zing! Curran cranks the pace back up and that's enough to send Stanlake packing, beats the bat and kisses the leg bail. And Australia have notched their lowest T20I total at home
taken at cover! Short of a length outside off, Salt drives off the back foot and you could hear the cry of 'oh, no' as that came off the splice
straight up, taken at mid-off! Short outside off, Brook swipes across the line, for a moment looks like Marsh might misjudge it at mid-off but he does well to track back and keep his eyes on it
another one! Short outside off, pace off at 119kph/73mph, Donald carves it square to cover point and Meredith is just making things interesting

28050.text: pitched up and punched in front of cover, they trot the two... England win by seven wickets, a thumping victory even without the DLS jiggery-pokery, to go 2-1 up in the series
28050.postText: 9.35pm: Here we go with the presentations... Starting with Player of the Match Jamie Overton: "Last couple of game I've been disappointed with the way I've bowled. We've not got a few experienced players here so it was a chance to step up. Nice to put in a performance today. [Catches] Try to contribute in the field, get in those hot spots. Maybe that helped today. We've done a lot of fitness and it's paying off at the moment. Keep working on it, try to be the fittest team we can be. [Hand injury?] Thumb's fine, just bit bruised." Australia's Mitch Marsh: "Very disappointing. We've got to own that. The Gabba's an excellent place to bat, some of our shot selection was off tonight. Don't want this young group to fear making mistakes but tonight was a chance to be a bit more calculated. No excuses, we've got to be better. You see it a lot in T20 cricket, think you need 200 to win the game. You can overplay that and get in trouble. We've all played Big Bash games here, give yourself the chance to cash in at the back end. But we didn't get near that tonight. Still excited about the talent in the group. Tonight was disappointing but still two games to go." England captain Harry Brook: "Unbelievable effort, thought Jamie Overton was outstanding tonight, he's worked hard and put in some extra graft at training. Simplified his game and reaped the rewards tonight. [Plans] Just trying to figure out the best mode of dismissal on that surface. He had it on a string and it felt like we could change the field and make them make a mistake. [Chance of series win] Phenomenal effort to come over here against a strong Australia and win in their back yard. Would be nice to finish it off in Sydney, got to stay present, stay in the moment and see what happens." Right, that's yer lot from Brizzy. Valkerie Baynes' report is incoming, and there'll be more to come during a busy period in world cricket - the Wellington Test, an Australia Test squad (with one headline omission), and another T20I in Sydney on Sunday. Until then, from myself, Gnasher and Chandan, it's good bye. Cheerio! 9.30pm: Yabba Gabba do. England get the job done with another statement win up in Queensland. It dribbled to a conclusion, which was a shame after Jamie Overton's five-for had dismantled Australia and then Aneurin Donald galloped off again in the chase

28040.text: smoked, third four in a row! Round the wicket, full outside off and crunched to the rope at deep cover
28040.postText: 9.26pm: The hessian was on for all of 30 seconds, I think. Off goes the buggy, the main covers folded away. Barely any rain on this occasion, and they're going to get on with it. Oh, and the target has been adjusted again: 93 from 16 now, another over lost during that unnecessary delay 9.23pm: Dearie me... it's raining again! England need seven to win and the groundstaff are scurrying out with the covers. Players on both sides are hanging around, keen to get this done now... And that seems to be what the umpires have said! Big cheer as the groundstaff are told to sling their hook

28030.text: one-handed slap for four! Back of a length and Cox goes for broke, hauls it away over the head of midwicket

28020.text: full and laced through the ring, a flowing drive from Cox that teases Marsh at mid-off before zipping away over the slick outfield

28010.preText: First change, Ben Dwarshuis on for Meredith
28010.text: dropped again! Pummelled back at the bowler, and Dwarshuis tried to hold it in front of his face. Fingertipped on to his own forehead, I think... Tough one, it came at him so quickly
28010.postText: He's going to get checked over by the medic. Just a glancing blow to his hairline... and Dwarshuis is okay to carry on

27070.text: short and swung away, Cox rides the bounce on the pull and gets four more wide of fine leg
27070.postText: "@Alan what happened to this Australian team? This is not the same team before that famous news comes back again. It's truly impacting on the team performance even at the familiar home grounds. How do you see?" Well, Vensee, they had already picked this squad before the "famous news" raised it's head again... T20Is bottom of the priority pile right now

27060.text: length ball, 133kph/82mph and hoicked away to deep square leg for one more

27050.text: back of a length, tapped behind square on the off side
27050.postText: Jamie Dow: "Nothing says you trust your bowling unit like..." To be fair to Bison, he's not blessed with options in this series

27040.text: slower ball, 112kph/69mph and nurdled leg side for one

27030.text: hoyed down the ground this time! Back of a length, 138kph but Cox is waiting, opens the shoulders to club four through the vacant long-on area

27020.text: blammed into the boards! Short ball, sits up nicely for the pull. Cox doesn't attempt to keep it down as he fetches six over deep midwicket

27010.text: short and fizzing down the leg side, wide signalled

26060.text: short of a length, 142kph/88mph and pulled to deep square leg
26060.postText: "Why is Jos Buttler not a part of T20 setup. Has he retired too?" Injured, Anirudh. Popped his hamstring during an ODI in September

26050.text: dropped! Chaudhary at backward point. Similar to his take off Donald, though this was full pace and came much quicker off the face of Cox's bat. Got the hands up, but it burst straight through

26040.text: fullish length, pace-on still, 141kph. Comes off the inside half of the bat and deflects off the pads for one

26030.text: stroked through extra cover, no issues with timing on this shot. Barely moves his feet but just lets the hands go and pings his drive

26020.text: hard length, 142kph/88mph and nipping back on off. Jabbed down into the deck

26010.preText: Away we go! Meredith to bowl his fourth straight through...
26010.text: full length and shaping away outside off, mistimed back into the on side
